claim: Each profile is signed up for one channel chosen from its owner's name, on top of email. So bob's profile, created after alice's, ends up with exactly two channels: email and the one his name maps to.
why: Profile copies DEFAULTS one level deep, so every profile shares one channels list, and += in enable extends that list in place. Which channel a name maps to comes from a SHA-256 digest, so only a run shows it: alice maps to push and bob to sms. Bob therefore ends with email, push and sms, three channels, not two.

deciding.note: bob also has push from alice, so not exactly two channels

root.claim: Bob's profile has exactly two channels: email and the one his name maps to.

atoms.claim: Bob's profile has exactly two channels, email and sms
atoms.evidence: Ran python3 main.py: it prints "bob light ['email', 'push', 'sms']". The channels list is shared across profiles, so alice's push is in bob's list.
Ran python3 -c with the SHA-256 digest of bob modulo 3: index 1, which is sms.
